page.overview:
Who is Araphant?

Araphant was the fourteenth King of Arthedain.

Araphant, the son and heir of King Araval, ascended to the throne in TA 1891 following his father's death. During his reign, the well-known seer Malbeth made a prediction regarding the fate of his son Arvedui, stating that he would be the last king of Arthedain; and as such, he advised Araphant to name his son Arvedui, meaning"last king". Malbeth's prophecy included a choice for the Dúnedain: if they took the less hopeful path, Arvedui would not change his name and would remain the last king, leading to much sorrow and many lives lost until the Dúnedain were united again.

For some five hundred years, Arthedain had held off the constant attacks of the evil realm of Angmar. Araphant continued fighting off these attacks with failing strength.

During his time, the rulers of Arthedain and Gondor became aware that a force was conducting coordinated attacks on the exiles of Númenor. Araphant therefore renewed contact with Gondor and forged an alliance with King Ondoher, leading to a marriage between Ondoher's daughter Fíriel and Araphant's son Arvedui. Four years later, King Ondoher died during an attack by the Wainriders, and Arvedui made a claim for the throne of Gondor by right of his blood connection to Isildur and his wife Fíriel, who by the laws of Númenor should have become the Ruling Queen. This claim was denied by Gondor, and the kingship of Gondor passed to Eärnil II.
